$comment: Client JS bundle-size budgets captured from a known-good production build. `production` guards aggregate user-facing chunks, `routes` guards the Lighthouse journeys and the main work-mode pages (added by the work-mode speed review, 7 Oct 2026) against route-local growth (route baselines lowered about 100 KB on 7 Oct 2026 (scaled from a local build by the ratio to the baselineSource build, so they stay comparable with it) when the sign-in library moved out of the first load, so that saving cannot quietly regrow), and `mockups` is a looser design-scratch hygiene ceiling. The `production` baseline alone was raised on 9 Oct 2026 to a local build of the hospital roles change merged with main (5472.8 KiB), after its 145 KiB duplicated-chunk regression was removed: main had already reached +9.8% from the combined work-mode growth. On 13 Oct 2026 the owner approved resetting two route baselines, /roster/shifts (390.9 KiB) and /teaching/assessments (459.3 KiB), to a local production build of main at f4bcb55a4. On 14 Oct 2026 PR #3538 (8f2a188ea4) refreshed baselines from main at f8f664425d4c (production 6,062,493 B, tightened mockups 670,993 B, totalGzipBytes 6,733,486 B, and the 13 monitored routes) after landing clinical math calculators, work search grammar, attendance roster, QR check-in helper, safe-number editor, and WA MHA print forms. Refresh intentionally with `npm run check:bundle-budget -- --update` and update this comment to cite the new baselineSource. On 26 Oct 2026 (performance audit M3) the routes were reordered so the Lighthouse journeys, now including /my-day, /on-call and /psychiatry/mha-clock, come first, and /psychiatry/mha-clock was added at 329,921 B from a local production build of claude/project-thread-6zvr2q at 4de2a4934 (other routes measured within 1.5% of their baselines in the same build); no other baseline changed. On 26 Oct 2026 (PR #3821) /roster and /open-shifts were moved up to follow /psychiatry/mha-clock so they match the Lighthouse journey order; only the key order changed, no baseline value.
